text: Né aseɛ te sesakaa bɔ olle bɔbea biala ɔ. Né awosii akata buma ne anye; na né Nyameɛ Sunzum natenate nzue ne anyeso faa.

text: Nyameɛ tole hyireinn ne dumaa Alehyeleɛ, yeɛ ɔtole awosii ne dumaa Alesaleɛ. Aleɛ sane, na aleɛ hyene: kyẽa bɔ oli moa ɛne.

text: Nyameɛ yɔle ewienu, na ɔtele nzue bɔ ɔwɔ ewienu bo fili bɔ ɔwɔ ewienu anwuro nwo.

text: Aseɛ fifili ndire, mmakaa bɔ osu mmaa, ɔne mmakaa bɔ mmaa wɔ ye aleɛ nu, ebiala kyɛbɔ ye sue si te ɔ. Na Nyameɛ nwuni kyɛ ɔte paa.

text: bɛɛyɛ nganea wɔ ewienu, ná bɛta aseɛ so!” Na ɔwale nu sɔ.

ref: Then God put these lights in the sky to shine on the earth,

text: Aleɛ sane, na aleɛ hyene: kyẽa bɔ ɔtɔ so nna ɛne.

ref: God said, “I command the ocean to be full of living creatures, and I command birds to fly above the earth.”
text: Na Nyameɛ hane kyɛ, “Nzue ɔlɔ abɔdeɛ ahoroɔ pee bɔ bele ngoa ɔ, ná nnomaa koso bétu bɛ́fa aseɛ so wɔ ewienu!”

ref: So God made the giant sea monsters and all the living creatures that swim in the ocean. He also made every kind of bird. God looked at what he had done, and it was good.

ref: Evening came, then morning—that was the fifth day. The Sixth Day
text: Aleɛ sane, na aleɛ hyene: kyẽa bɔ ɔtɔ so nnu ɛne.

text: Yiti Nyameɛ bɔle sona kyɛ ye bɔbɔ ye sɛso, Nyameɛ sɛso yeɛ ɔbɔle ye ɔ; ɔbɔle bienzua ne brasua.

ref: And I have given the green plants as food for everything else that breathes, including animals, both wild and tame, and birds. And so it was.

text: Yiti sɔ yeɛ Nyameɛ bɔle anwuro ne aseɛ ne bɛ nu nningyein mukoraa yiele ɔ.

ref: The Lord made a garden in a place called Eden, which was in the east, and he put the man there.

ref: The Lord God filled the garden with all kinds of beautiful trees and fruit trees. Two other trees were in the middle of the garden. One of these gave life—the other gave the wisdom to know the difference between right and wrong.
text: Na AWURADE Nyameɛ mane mmakaa mukoraa bɔ bɛyɛ nyemene ná ɔte paa kyɛ bedi ɔ fifili aseɛnwo wɔ turo ne anu; ɔmane ngoa bakaa fifili turo n’afia, yeɛ paa ne bɔne nwo nimdeɛ bakaa koso fifili nu.

ref: The Lord God put the man in the Garden of Eden to take care of it and to look after it.

ref: But the Lord told him, “You may eat fruit from any tree in the garden,

ref: the Lord made a woman out of the rib. The Lord God brought her to the man,

ref: That's why a man will leave his own father and mother. He marries a woman, and the two of them become like one person.
text: Yiti bienzua kofi ɔse ne oni anwo, ná waafa ye nwo wabata ɔye, na bayɛ anwoɔnaen ko.

text: Nakoso ewoo ne sele braa ne kyɛ, “Ɛmɔngowu biala.

ref: Late in the afternoon, when the breeze began to blow, the man and woman heard the Lord God walking in the garden. So they hid behind some trees. Sin Brings a Curse

text: Na braa ne wora, Nyameɛ sele ye kyɛ, “Ngɔmaa ɛkɔte aworɛ nu yealɛ paa, na yealɛ nu yeɛ ɛkɔwo mmaa ɔ. Nakoso wɔ wora kɔlɔ ehu, na okoli wɔ so.”

text: Nyameɛ ɔ́ma Yafɛte boso ɔ́trɛ, ɔ́ma ɔtena Sem ɛtena sua nu, ná ɔma Kanaan ɔyɛ Yafɛte kanganiɛ.”

ref: After the flood Shem, Ham, and Japheth had many descendants. The Descendants of Japheth
text: Nowa mma mmienzua Sem, Ham ne Yafɛte bɛ boso ama ɛhe: Nzueyilɛ ne asi ne, bɛwole mmaa.

ref: Japheth's descendants had their own languages, tribes, and land. They were Gomer, Magog, Madai, Javan, Tubal, Meshech, and Tiras. Gomer was the ancestor of Ashkenaz, Riphath, and Togarmah. Javan was the ancestor of Elishah, Tarshish, Kittim, and Dodanim, who settled along the coast. The Descendants of Ham
text: Bɛ boso ama ole mmenia bɔ bato bapete mboanoa aseɛ so ne. Yafɛte mma mɔ bɔ bɛwɔ b’aseɛ so ɛhe: asora fekue biala ne ye dwudwolɛ, ye abusua ne ye maen.

ref: This completes the list of Noah's descendants. After the flood their descendants became nations and spread all over the world.
text: Nowa mma nemɔ b’abusua, kyɛbɔ b’aworɛ ndoatoasoɛ te wɔ bɛ maen nu ɛhe. Na ofi bɛ nu yeɛ nzueyilɛ ne asi ne maen maen fifili na bɛto bɛpetene aseɛ so ɔ.

ref: but after some of them moved from the east and settled in Babylonia,
text: Mmerɛ bɔ mmenia tu fili eyia afiteleɛ nen, benwuni aseɛ frɛtɛɛ bie wɔ Sinari aseɛ so, na bɛtenane berɛ.

ref: they said: Let's build a city with a tower that reaches to the sky! We'll use hard bricks and tar instead of stone and mortar. We'll become famous, and we won't be scattered all over the world.
text: Afei besele kyɛ, “Biamɔ, ɛ́mɔma yɛkyekye yɛ kuro, ná yɛsi abandenden bɔ odwu nyameɛso yɛsie so, ná yɛfa yɛle dumaa, amaa yammɔ aya wɔ aseɛ ye aso amukoraa.”

ref: But when the Lord came down to look at the city and the tower,
text: AWURADE dwu wale ase ɔɔneane kuro ne abandenden bɔ né mmenia mmaa bési ne.

ref: he said: These people are working together because they all speak the same language. This is just the beginning. Soon they will be able to do anything they want.
text: Na AWURADE sele kyɛ, “Bɛte mmenia komapɛ, na bɛ mukoraa bɛka edwudwolɛ ko. Ɔ́hyɛ ye bo ye po yeɛ bɛ́yɔ sɔaa ye. Nzaade bɔ bekosusu kyɛ bɛkɔyɔ biala ne, nikye fee ngosi bɛ ate.

ref: Let's go down and confuse them! We'll make them speak different languages, and they won't be able to understand each other.
text: Ɛmɔbra, ɛ́mɔma yɛdwu yɛhɔ ase, ná yɛkakyi bɛ dwudwolɛ ne ma ɔyɛ nwunyaenn, amaa bɛ nu biala ande obiɛngo dwudwolɛ bo ko.”

ref: So the people had to stop building the city, because the Lord confused their language and scattered them all over the earth. That's how the city of Babel got its name. The Descendants of Shem
text: Ɛhe ati yeɛ ɔmaa bɛfrɛ berɛ Babɛl, ofikyɛ AWURADE mane aseɛ so amukoraa dwudwolɛ yɛle nwunyaenn. Na ofi sɔ mmerɛ ne, AWURADE maa bɛbɔle aya wɔ aseɛ ye aso amukoraa. Sem boso ama (

text: Na Seruge wole Nahɔ nen, ye si ye olili afoɛ ɛyaa nyɔ, na ɔwole mmaa mmienzua ne mmrasua mɔ koso.

ref: Terah decided to move from Ur to the land of Canaan. He took along Abram and Sarai and his grandson Lot, the son of Haran. But when they came to the city of Haran, they settled there instead.
text: Tera fale ɔwa Abram, ye anomaa Lɔto bɔ ɔte Haran awa ne, ye sia Sarae bɔ ɔte ɔwa Abram aye ne, na ɔne bɛ betu befili Yure bɔ ɔwɔ Kaldea kyɛ bɛ́kɔ Kanaan aseɛ so. Nakoso bedwuli Haran nen, bɛtenane berɛ.

ref: The Lord said to Abram: Leave your country, your family, and your relatives and go to the land that I will show you.
text: Na AWURADE sele Abram kyɛ, “Tu fi wɔ maen nu, w’abusuafoɛ nu, ɔne ɛse awuro, ná kɔ aseɛ bɔ mebaahyire wɔ ne aso.

ref: I will bless you and make your descendants into a great nation. You will become famous and be a blessing to others.
text: Ngɔmaa ɛkɔyɛ maen pirikua, ngoyira wɔ, ná mama wɔ dumaa ahɔ anwuro, amaa ɔnate so ayɛ saleɛ.

ref: I will bless those who bless you, but I will put a curse on anyone who puts a curse on you. Everyone on earth will be blessed because of you.
text: Ngoyira bɛ bɔ beyira wɔ, na ebiala bɔ ɔnoma wɔ ne, me koso ngɔnoma ye; na ɔnate wɔ so yeɛ aseɛ so mmusua amukoraa bekonya saleɛ ɔ.”

ref: Abram went as far as the sacred tree of Moreh in a place called Shechem. The Canaanites were still living in the land at that time,
text: Abram pɛle nu wɔ aseɛ ne aso, na oodwuli More eluii bakaa bɔ ɔwɔ Sɛkem ne anwo. Sɔ mmerɛ ne, né Kanaanfoɛ wɔ aseɛ ne aso.

ref: but the Lord appeared to Abram and promised, “I will give this land to your family forever.” Abram then built an altar there for the Lord.
text: Na AWURADE yele ye nwo ali hyirele Abram, na osele kyɛ, “Wɔ bosofoɛ yeɛ ngɔfa sɔ aseɛ he ngɔma bɛ ɔ.” Yiti Abram sili afɔleɛ bokyea berɛ mane AWURADE bɔ ɔyele ye nwo ali hyirele ye ne.

ref: Abram traveled to the hill country east of Bethel and camped between Bethel and Ai, where he built another altar and worshiped the Lord.
text: Afei otu fili berɛ hɔle mmokaa aseɛ bɔ ɔwɔ Betel eyia afiteleɛ ne aso dɔ, na osili ye ɛtena sua wɔ berɛ; bɔ né Betel wɔ ye eyia atɔleɛ, yeɛ Aye koso wɔ ye eyia afiteleɛ. Osili afɔleɛ bokyea berɛ mane AWURADE, na ɔsɔnene AWURADE.

ref: Later, Abram started out toward the Southern Desert. Abram in Egypt
text: Abram toale ye ateetulɛ ne aso fale ye nye hyirele ngwaen dɔ aseɛ ne. Abram wɔ Misraim

ref: The crops failed, and there was no food anywhere in Canaan. So Abram and his wife Sarai went to live in Egypt for a while. But just before they got there, Abram said, “Sarai, you are really beautiful!
text: Na ɔka kãa maa odwu Misraim nen, osele ɔye Sarae kyɛ, “Mese kyɛ ɛte brasua bɔ wɔ nwo yɛ nyemene ɔ;

ref: When the Egyptians see you, they will murder me because I am your husband. But they won't kill you.
text: na sɛ Misraimfoɛ nwu wɔ a, bɛkɔhã kyɛ, ‘Ɔye ɔ’; ná bahu me, nakoso wɔ de bɛkɔyakyi wɔ.

ref: As soon as Abram and Sarai arrived in Egypt, the Egyptians noticed how beautiful she was.
text: Abram dwuli Misraim nen, Misraimfoɛ nemɔ nwuni kyɛ braa ne nwo yɛ nyemene paa.

ref: The king's officials told him about her, and she was taken to his house.
text: Faro mbanyi nemɔ nwuni ye, na bɛkamvole ye behyirele Faro. Na bɛfale braa ne bɛhɔle Faro awuro.

ref: The king was good to Abram because of Sarai, and Abram was given sheep, cattle, donkeys, slaves, and camels.
text: Na ɔnate ye ti Faro lele Abram nyemene so; na Abram nyane mmoaen, nandwie, afunum nyii mɔ, ngoaa ne afaneɛ mɔ, afunum beleɛ mɔ ne afupɔngɔ mɔ.

ref: Because of Sarai, the Lord struck the king and everyone in his palace with terrible diseases.
text: Na ɔnate Abram aye Sarae ti, AWURADE fale amaneɛ pirikua tole Faro ne ye awuro ama so.

ref: Finally, the king sent for Abram and said to him, “What have you done to me? Why didn't you tell me Sarai was your wife?
text: Yiti Faro frɛle Abram bisale ye kyɛ, “Nzikyɛ dwirɛ paa yeɛ afa ali me e? Nzu ati yeɛ anga angyire me kyɛ ɛye ahɔ ɔ?

ref: Why did you make me believe she was your sister? Now I've married her. Take her and go! She's your wife.”
text: Nzu ati yeɛ ɛhane kyɛ ‘Nniɛma ɔ,’ bɔ ahaa ɛmaa mefa ye meyɛ me ye ɔ? Nea, ɛye ne ɛhe. Fa ye na ɛne ye befi wa bɛhɔ!”

ref: So the king told his men to let Abram and Sarai take their possessions and leave.
text: Na Faro hyɛle mmenia kyɛ bɛma Abram ɔhɔ, na bɛhane Abram ne ɔye, ɔne bɔ banya ye amukoraa beguale atee so maa bɛhɔle.

ref: Abram and Sarai took everything they owned and went to the Southern Desert. Lot went with them.
text: Yiti Abram fili Misraim hɔle ngwaen dɔ aseɛ ne aso dɔ, ɔne ɔye ne bɔ wanya ye amukoraa, na Lɔto ne ye bɛhɔle.

ref: Abram was very rich. He owned many cattle, sheep, and goats, and had a lot of silver and gold.
text: Né Abram anya ye nwo tam wɔ nyɛmmoa, ɛdwetɛ ne sikaa kɔkorɛ nu.

ref: Abram moved from place to place in the Southern Desert. And finally, he went north and set up his tents between Bethel and Ai,
text: Olili tutena toonn fili ngwaen dɔ aseɛ ne aso oodwuli Betel, na odwuli nekaa bɔ olili moa sili ye ɛtena sua ne, wɔ Betel ne Aye b’afia.

ref: where he had earlier camped and built an altar. There he worshiped the Lord.
text: Oodwuli nekaa bɔ olili moa sili afɔleɛ bokyea ne. Na Abram sɔnene AWURADE berɛ.

ref: Lot, who was traveling with him, also had sheep, goats, and cattle, as well as his own family and slaves.
text: Né Lɔto bɔ ɔne Abram bɛnate ne koso ole mmoaen ne nandwie ne ɛtena sua mɔ.

ref: At this time the Canaanites and the Perizzites were still living in the same area, and so there wasn't enough pastureland left for Abram and Lot with all of their animals. Besides this, the men who took care of Abram's animals and the ones who took care of Lot's animals started quarreling.
text: Na edwudwolɛ wale Abram ngaka neafoɛ nemɔ ne Lɔto ngaka neafoɛ nemɔ afia. Na sɔ mmerɛ ne, né Kanaanfoɛ ne Perisifoɛ wɔ sɔ aseɛ ne aso.

ref: Abram said to Lot, “We are close relatives. We shouldn't argue, and our men shouldn't be fighting one another.
text: Na Abram sele Lɔto kyɛ, “Mesrɛ wɔ, nnɛma aporowaa biala ba me ne wɔ afia, ɔne wɔ ngaka neafoɛ ne me ngaka neafoɛ afia, ofikyɛ yɛbɔ abusua.
